text: The horse, the stable, its people and the country round
why: The favourite, its trainer and the setting at King's Pyland on Dartmoor are all mentioned; a stable of the trainer is a reasonable inference.

text: The searchers' account: the lads roused, the knoll, the coat, the body
why: Lads, a knoll and a coat are never mentioned; the story only says the trainer was murdered, not how the body was found.

text: What the police found: the wounds, the hands, the hollow, the hunt for the horse
why: The wounds, hands and hollow are not mentioned, and no police finds are described; the story only reports a disappearance and a murder.
The story says the trainer of the favourite was murdered.
Holmes's news agent sent up fresh editions of the papers.
The favourite for the Wessex Cup has disappeared.
Holmes and Watson are at breakfast and Holmes rambles about the room, so the rooms are established.
Holmes charges and recharges his pipe with black tobacco.
Fresh editions of every paper were sent up and tossed aside.
The case is the one topic of conversation across England and a problem before the public.

text: Who struck the blow that killed Straker?
why: The name Straker has not been used, and the story does not yet say the trainer was struck by a blow; the question's wording presupposes both.
